papers.abstract: We prove the global nonlinear stability of small planar contact waves for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\R^3$ under general $H^4(\R^3)$ perturbations, without any $L^1$ integrability or zero-mass assumptions. Unlike the one-dimensional problem or the periodic channel, the problem in $\R^3$ admits neither a Poincaré inequality in the transverse directions nor a square-integrable anti-derivative. Our proof relies on three main ingredients: a perturbation around the one-dimensional Navier--Stokes solution starting from the smooth contact profile, a formulation of the low-order perturbation system in the velocity, pressure, and entropy variables with separate estimates for the velocity--pressure pair and the entropy, and the construction of characteristic and space-time Gaussian weight functions. Combining these weighted estimates with higher-order derivative bounds and homogeneous Gagliardo--Nirenberg interpolation yields global stability and algebraic $L^\infty$ decay rates in $\R^3$.

papers.title: Scalable Estimation and Inference for Varying Coefficient Expectile Regression with Streaming Data
papers.abstract: Nonparametric expectile regression methods face new challenges from streaming data, where retaining the full dataset for batch processing becomes increasingly impractical. In this paper, we develop a scalable nonparametric expectile regression framework for varying coefficient models. We estimate the coefficient functions online via functional stochastic gradient descent with Polyak--Ruppert averaging in a product reproducing kernel Hilbert space, requiring only gradient information and one pass over the data. For this online estimator, we establish non-asymptotic error bounds, prove its optimal nonparametric convergence rate under the proposed step-size schemes, and derive its Berry--Esseen bound for pointwise asymptotic normality. To perform online inference for the varying coefficient expectile regression models, we propose a multiplier bootstrap procedure that perturbs the stochastic gradients with independent random weights and recursively constructs bootstrap trajectories. We establish the bootstrap consistency of the online inference procedure, yielding asymptotically valid pointwise confidence intervals. Simulation studies and a real data application confirm the performance of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Thermal Field Theory for General Equilibrium Density Matrices
papers.abstract: Thermal field theory (TFT) is the combination of statistical mechanics and relativistic quantum field theory. This (book) chapter provides a pedagogical introduction to (and a review of) TFT for general equilibrium density matrices, which allow arbitrary values not only of temperature and chemical potentials, but also of average angular momentum. A general technique to compute ensemble averages is illustrated. Path-integral methods are developed to study the partition function and the thermal Green's functions of general operators, with an arbitrary number of points, in all field theories of physical relevance.

papers.title: Well-posedness of weak solutions for the time-dependent thermal-fluid-solid multiphysical coupled model
papers.abstract: This paper constructs a time-dependent thermal-fluid-solid multiphysical coupled model describing the interaction between a free fluid and a thermo-poroelastic medium and provides a rigorous mathematical analysis. The model consists of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations and the heat equation in the free-fluid region, together with the thermo-poroelasticity equations in the porous medium. The two regions are coupled on a fixed interface through conditions for normal velocity, tangential velocity, stress balance, temperature continuity, and heat flux continuity. Under a small-data assumption, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a weak solution for this fully dynamic nonlinear coupled system. The proof employs the Galerkin method to construct semi-discrete approximations, establishes uniform a priori estimates that enable the extension of local solutions to global ones, and invokes compactness arguments to pass to the limit, yielding a solution to the original coupled system.

papers.title: A hair-thin implant opens the entire depth of the mouse brain to revisiting the same structures at subcellular resolution
papers.abstract: Ultrathin multimode-fibre endoscopes provide minimally invasive access to subcellular structures throughout the depth of the mouse brain. Here we introduce a chronically implantable interface with a diameter of 144 μm, about the thickness of a human hair, that extends this capability to longitudinal imaging, enabling repeated access to the same fine structures over extended periods. The system supports weeks-long tracking of individual dendritic spines, allowing quantitative comparison of their dynamics and survival across dendritic compartments. We further demonstrate longitudinal intracellular calcium imaging during spontaneous and stimulus-evoked activity in the same cells across days, as well as repeated measurements of blood flow in the same vessels across multiple brain regions. This chronic endomicroscopic platform provides stable, minimally invasive optical access for longitudinal subcellular-resolution imaging of brain structure, activity and blood flow across depth.

papers.title: Rigid continua containing an arbitrary Peano continuum
papers.abstract: Bani\v c and Kac, and later \v Crepnjak and Kac, constructed an uncountable family of continua with different types of rigidity. For every continuum $X$ with the mentioned property, the inverse limit $\varprojlim\{X,f_n\}$ is homeomorphic to $X$ for an arbitrary sequence of continuous surjective functions $f_n: X \to X$. We extend these results by proving that for any Peano continuum $X$ there exists an uncountable family ${\cal F}$ of rigid, for each positive integer $m$, $\frac{1}{m}$-rigid, and $0$-rigid continua such that each $Y \in {\cal F}$ contains a homeomorphic copy of $X$ and for each $Y \in {\cal F}$ it holds that the inverse limit $\varprojlim\{Y,f_n\}$ is homeomorphic to $Y$ for arbitrarily sequence of continuous surjective functions $f_n: Y \to Y$.

papers.title: Resolving non-neutrality across scales in a hyperdiverse tropical forest
papers.abstract: Different ecological processes operate at different spatial and temporal scales. Macroscopic regularities can therefore be captured by descriptions that ignore microscopic details, even when those details are mechanistically relevant to ecological processes. Here, we develop a framework inspired by statistical mechanics to track interspecific spatial correlations under spatial coarse-graining. To do so we combine random-matrix filtering with a spatially explicit neutral model. Applying this approach to eight censuses of the Barro Colorado Island tropical forest, we observe a continuous crossover from an interacting to an effectively neutral organization. Below a few tens of metres (20--35~m), the empirical correlation spectrum differs from neutral expectations, revealing scale-dependent species-specific structure. Part of this structure can be attributed to environmental heterogeneity. However, residual spatial associations provide candidate signatures of biotic interactions or other unmeasured ecological, non-neutral processes. With increasing spatial coarse-graining, empirical and neutral correlation spectra progressively converge, and above the crossover scale the neutral model provides an accurate description of the measured collective organization. Neutrality thus emerges as an effective description of the collective organization of the forest above a characteristic scale, without implying that species are equivalent at the individual level. Our framework provides an operational way to locate that scale.

papers.title: An interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles
papers.abstract: We conjecture a novel interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles: $θ^{}_{23} = \left(θ^{}_{12} + θ^{}_{13}\right)/2 + π/8$, which predicts $θ^{}_{23} = 43.46^{+0.51^\circ}_{-0.52^\circ}$ with inputs of the latest JUNO and Daya Bay precision data. A simple ansatz is proposed to derive this phenomenologically favored and experimentally testable angle relation, and present a new expansion of the lepton flavor mixing matrix in powers of a single small parameter as a by-product.

papers.title: Sharp universality thresholds for random profinite groups
papers.abstract: We determine sharp universality thresholds for quotients of the free profinite group $\widehat F_n$ on $n$ generators by $n+u$ independent random relations, where $u$ is a fixed nonnegative integer. For products of mutually independent uniformly coset-balanced factors, convergence to the Liu--Wood measure $μ_u$ holds when the minimum number of factors grows faster than $\log n$, which is a uniformly sharp condition. For random words of fixed length $\ell_n$, convergence holds exactly when $\ell_n$ is eventually odd and $\ell_n-\log n\to\infty$. We also prove universality for randomly ordered products of independent integer powers under the balance condition $nα_{n,p}/\log n\to\infty$ at each fixed prime, recovering finite-prime cokernel laws by abelianization.

papers.title: LEMMO: A Large Electromagnetic Model leveraging Pretrained LLMs for Million-Sample Signal Understanding
papers.abstract: Large language models have expanded beyond text to vision, audio, and other modalities, but understanding raw electromagnetic (EM) signals remains challenging. Wideband recordings can contain millions of samples, whereas existing waveform-based EM models are primarily evaluated on short in-phase and quadrature (IQ) segments, leaving long-recording understanding and detailed description insufficiently explored. We introduce LEMMO, a large EM model for instruction-driven recognition and description of long raw IQ recordings. LEMMO combines a linear-attention EM encoder with anti-aliased temporal resampling to process up to eight million complex samples. Its EM-text interaction module conditions learnable queries on instructions before retrieving signal evidence. Compact queries support recognition, while structured queries with auxiliary factual supervision organize scene-level properties, signal attributes, and cross-signal relationships for detailed description. We also construct and release a unified 1.38-TB corpus of real-world and synthetic EM signals, including LEMMO-ShortQA and LEMMO-LongDesc. Compared with MERLIN-LoRA, LEMMO improves mean EM-Bench perception accuracy by 15.77 %, mean strategy-generation ROUGE-L F1 by 4.38 points, and mean LEMMO-ShortQA accuracy by 14.31 %. It also improves categorical and numerical fact F1 on both LEMMO-LongDesc tasks while preserving its language backbone's MMLU performance. Our code and datasets are available at https://github.com/N1rv4n4/LEMMO and https://huggingface.co/datasets/DaftJun/RFLAS, respectively.

papers.title: Validation of Habitable Zone Limits with a New Radiative-Convective Equilibrium Climate Model
papers.abstract: The habitable zone (HZ) boundaries calculated with the Clima one-dimensional radiative-convective equilibrium (RCE) model have served as a standard reference for exoplanet target selection for three decades, but they have never been independently validated with a comparable model. We present ExoColumn, a new one-dimensional RCE model that couples an independently developed atmospheric column physics package to the ExoRT correlated-k radiative transfer core that is also used by the three-dimensional ExoCAM model. We calibrate ExoColumn to present-day conditions, which matches other RCE models to within a few kelvin through the troposphere. Line-by-line benchmarks show that the ExoRT and Clima radiation cores each reproduce the outgoing longwave flux to within a few percent, with the differences due to the spectral line databases used by each model. We follow the same inverse climate modeling method as previous studies have done to find inner edge moist- and runaway-greenhouse limits of 0.970 au and 0.966 au, and an outer-edge maximum-greenhouse limit of 1.611 au at a CO$_2$ partial pressure of 8.7 bar. We extend these calculations to 12 host stars spanning 2000-7200 K and to planets of 0.1, 1, and 5 Earth mass, and we provide updated HZ boundary coefficients for community use. The ExoColumn limits systematically fall closer to the host star than those of Clima but agree to within a few percent in orbital distance, which validates the robustness of the published Clima HZ boundaries.

papers.title: Nebula: Distributed Position-Independent Caching for LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Modern LLM workflows, such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and LLM agents, build long prompts from multiple independent text segments, making prefill a major source of computation. Reusing KV caches is therefore important for reducing serving costs and latency: distributed caching systems spread KV cache across a cluster to increase aggregate capacity, while position-independent caching (PIC) enables reuse of recurring segments under different prefixes. However, existing systems distribute KV caches but still rely on prefix caching (PC), while existing PIC methods enable position-independent reuse without cluster-wide resource management. We present Nebula, the first distributed LLM serving framework to treat PIC segments as first-class citizens, enabling remote PIC reuse and parallel prefill. To track PIC's fine-grained, asynchronous state changes, Nebula combines optimistic accounting with event-driven updates to provide a timely and truthful cluster view for cache management and prefill scheduling. To accommodate diverse reuse patterns across workloads, Nebula leverages cluster-wide ghost-hit feedback to automatically tune the allocation of shared cache capacity between PC and PIC. Finally, Nebula incorporates queueing, computation, and KV transfer costs into a unified prefill completion time model to guide elastic parallelism adjustment and locality-aware compute placement. Across four models and four real-world RAG and agentic workloads, Nebula reduces median TTFT by an average of 61.4% compared with the strongest existing baseline and recovers an average of 76.1% of the tokens missed by prefix caching.

papers.title: Stacking, symmetry and exciton fine structure in boron nitride bilayers
papers.abstract: Engineering of two-dimensional material heterostructures offers a broad range of degrees of freedom through the selection of type and number of layers and their relative stacking configurations. In these compound materials, the stacking sequence plays a central role in determining electronic, mechanical, and optical properties. Here, we present a theoretical study of its signature on the excitons of hexagonal boron nitride bilayers based on first-principle calculations within the GW approximation and the Bethe-Salpeter equation. We explain how stacking-dependent symmetry variations lead to distinct electronic structures, particularly near the band edge around the K high-symmetry point, and consequently to markedly different excitonic landscapes. Indeed, we analyze the symmetry-governed character of the low-lying excitonic states, identifying their bright or dark nature for each stacking configuration and performing a systematic comparison. Our results clarify how van der Waals interlayer coupling reshapes excitons in hexagonal boron nitride bilayers and outline prospects for twist-controlled exciton engineering in this material.

papers.title: ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation
papers.abstract: Language-model agents use experience through external retrieval and parameter learning. Consolidating stored experience into model weights requires deciding both which experience to train on and when its external records can leave retrieval. Admission based solely on student mastery can exclude useful teacher demonstrations, while removal immediately after training can discard guidance that the model still needs. We introduce ENGRAM, a framework that separates training admission from memory release. A demonstration-aware gate admits skills based on student mastery or sufficient successful teacher demonstrations. The student learns from selected action traces with context from an Engram Trace Graph (ETG). A verification gate then compares the updated model without episodic retrieval against the base model with retrieval on reserved probes. Release requires valid training participation and scores meeting both relative and absolute criteria; records for skills that fail verification remain retrievable. Experiments across interactive and reasoning benchmarks show consistent gains over frozen-weight ETG controls, with ablations supporting demonstration-aware admission and selective adapter activation. A controlled held-out comparison shows that verified release substantially reduces the retrievable footprint while remaining close to retain-all performance and outperforming immediate and budget-matched random release. ENGRAM also improves task performance while reducing input-token usage and model calls. Skill-level verification further reduces retrievable experience through selective archival, retaining external guidance for skills that do not meet the release criteria. Code is available in anonymous.4open.science/r/engram-anonymous.

papers.title: Interface-driven second harmonic generation in indium tin oxide/gold nanolayers: density and mass discontinuities matter
papers.abstract: Second harmonic generation from transparent conductive oxides and metals is traditionally attributed to Coulomb, magnetic Lorentz, and convective sources. We show that this picture is incomplete in deeply subwavelength indium tin oxide/gold bilayers. Measurements reveal two robust spectral features, a broad maximum near 1000 nm and an epsilon-near-zero peak near 1350 nm, that persist across wide variations in material and excitation parameters. Hydrodynamic-Maxwell simulations identify an interface-specific convective mechanism activated by freeelectron density and effective-mass discontinuities at the oxide-metal boundary. As electronic homogenization develops across the bilayer, the response evolves toward one described by conventional Coulomb, Lorentz, and leading convective terms. These results establish second harmonic generation as a sensitive probe of interface-driven nonlinearities and suggest a broader role for electronic discontinuities in shaping nonlinear optical processes at surface and buried material interfaces.

papers.title: Consensus-Constrained Dual-Federated Optimization with Client-Side Dynamic Weighting for Distributed Android Device Threat Defense
papers.abstract: Smartphones, smart-home hubs, and wearables are increasingly exposed to sophisticated Android malware, while centralized threat-detection pipelines raise privacy and scalability concerns. Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without collecting raw client data, but partial participation and variation in local model quality can destabilize global optimization. In this article, we propose DW-FedADMM, a federated optimization framework that combines primal-dual coordination with performance-dependent client-side weighting. The dynamic coefficient modulates each participating client's local state before the augmented-Lagrangian update, while the dual variables regulate disagreement between local and global model states. We evaluate DW-FedADMM on three Android malware benchmarks, namely Drebin, Malgenome, and TUANDROMD, with 5, 10, and 15 clients holding IID data shards, partial client participation, and communication budgets of 5 and 10 rounds. Each configuration is repeated with ten random seeds. DW-FedADMM obtains the highest seed-averaged accuracy on Drebin (97.64% +/- 0.20%) and the best mean accuracy in 9 of the 18 dataset-client-round configurations, including 7 of the 9 configurations with a 10-round budget. Pooled over all configurations, it reaches 95.42% accuracy, 94.62% F1-score, 96.06% precision, and 99.45% AUC, compared with 95.32%, 94.51%, 95.56%, and 99.41% for FedADMM, while also giving the lowest mean false-positive rate and the smallest client update norm among the six compared methods. Both primal-dual methods are well ahead of the averaging- and proximal-based baselines on Malgenome and TUANDROMD, where the latter often remain at the majority-class solution when clients are fragmented. The gain of dynamic weighting over FedADMM is most pronounced on Drebin and with the longer communication budget, where it also reduces the variation across seeds.

papers.title: Coexistence of antiferromagnetism and topological $s+d+id$ superconductivity in twisted cuprate bilayers
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between antiferromagnetism and topological superconductivity in twisted cuprate bilayers. We demonstrate how topological $s+d+id$ superconductivity is induced by a twist of $θ\sim 45^\circ$ in a microscopic $t$-$J$ type model of cuprate bilayers, where it robustly coexists with antiferromagnetic order at low hole doping. This novel pairing state becomes physically accessible at realistic interlayer couplings in the overdoped regime. Crucially, it displays a characteristic $2$-fold rotational symmetry in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) not observed in the competing time-reversal symmetry breaking $d+id$ or $s+id$ states previously found. A finite Josephson effect at $45^\circ$ twist together with signatures in scanning tunneling spectroscopy of its two Majorana edge modes identifies this topological $s+d+id$ state unambiguously.

papers.title: Mechanical Interaction Sensing for Robotic Kiwifruit Handling with an Optoelectronic Soft Suction Cup
papers.abstract: Robotic handling of delicate fruit benefits from compliant contact and quantitative sensing of the mechanical interaction at the end-effector. This study investigates an optoelectronic soft suction cup with a kiwifruit-specific bicomponent design for estimating interaction forces during contact with real fruit. During known-contact intervals, the optical signals accurately estimate interaction force on fruits excluded from model training: the best shallow network achieves grouped out-of-fold pooled R-squared = 0.968 +/- 0.005 (MAE = 0.138 N), with a median per-fruit held-out R-squared = 0.973 (MAE = 0.134 N). A simple monotonic mapping from the mean optical response alone achieves R-squared = 0.925 +/- 0.005, showing that substantial force-related information is already present in the optical response. Leave-one-collection-day-out validation remains strong (R-squared = 0.955 +/- 0.031), supporting robustness across acquisition sessions. As an exploratory secondary analysis, binary Soft/Firm classification from compression-test reference labels achieves moderate balanced accuracy (approximately 0.705) under grouped held-out-fruit validation, while finer three-class grading shows limited performance.

papers.title: Ahlfors $1$-Regularity and Conformal Criteria for Carleson Measures
papers.abstract: We prove that a bounded Jordan domain $Ω$ has Ahlfors $1$-regular boundary if and only if the following criterion holds for every positive Borel measure $μ$ on $Ω$: $μ$ is Carleson exactly when $\int_Ω|ϕ'(w)|\,dμ(w)<\infty$ for every conformal bijection $ϕ$ from $Ω$ onto a bounded domain with rectifiable boundary. The same characterization holds using only arclength measures on simple locally rectifiable curves, with the integral condition replaced by finite length of every such conformal image. These results extend Bishop's theorem on the unit disk. We also study analogous criteria for vanishing Carleson measures.

papers.title: Symmetry Breaking over Multiway Channels
papers.abstract: Identical users running the same algorithm must often break their symmetry and agree on distinct roles, as in leader election, naming, and resource allocation. We study anonymous symmetry breaking over a discrete memoryless multiway channel invariant under permutations of its $J$ users: each user observes only a private output and must choose a number in $\{1,\dots,J\}$, and the symmetry is broken if the $J$ numbers are distinct. Using a Rényi change of measure, we derive a finite-blocklength converse on the error probability of every symmetric causal protocol, including adaptive and randomized ones. For achievability, block coding with random names reduces the problem to all-source multicast, for which we derive a Gallager random-coding exponent for every fixed $J$, and a cut-set bound that limits the exponent of the probability that two names coincide or are decoded wrongly. Interactive role controllers instead let the users contend for identifiers directly: we give their exact error probability, an achievable exponent given by a spectral radius when some outputs certify a role, and a floor for finite-state controllers when every output has positive probability, and we introduce generalized musical chairs. On a noisy bandit channel motivated by multiplayer multi-armed bandits, with noiseless collisions and arms of a common mean below one, interactive schemes provably exceed the limit of name decoding, and numerical estimates suggest the same with noisy collisions. For two users, noiseless collisions, one informative arm and a silent arm, the optimal error probability is determined up to a factor of two.

papers.title: Two-step nilpotent varieties as categories of modules over a square ring
papers.abstract: We characterise the two-step nilpotent varieties of algebras: the semi-abelian varieties in which all ternary cosmash products vanish. Just as abelian varieties are the categories of modules over a ring, two-step nilpotent varieties are exactly the categories of modules over a square ring in the sense of Baues, Hartl and Pirashvili. We construct the square ring explicitly from the full subcategory on the free algebras on one and two generators, and give complete proofs. As consequences we obtain a description of any two-step nilpotent variety by generators and relations, an intrinsic characterisation in terms of quadratic term operations, and an account of its abelian core and of the lower central series of its objects in terms of the square ring. Along the way, we associate with any commutative ring $R$ a square ring whose modules, the two-step nilpotent $R$-groups, extend Hall's nilpotent $R$-groups of class two from $2$-binomial rings to arbitrary rings of coefficients.

papers.title: Dynamics and pseudospectra around quantum exceptional points
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) are a hallmark of non-Hermitian physics, giving rise to extreme sensitivity and enhanced dynamic response. Such unique spectral singularities have been extensively studied in classical photonics, both at theoretical and experimental levels, where the relevant observables are evident. That is not necessarily the case in the quantum regime, where this kind of behavior around EPs, to a large extent, remains elusive. In fact, the interplay between dissipation and quantum fluctuations makes the complete Lindbladian evolution quite different from effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian descriptions. In this context, we investigate the signatures of the Liouvillian EPs on spectral and dynamic response by considering properly normalized long-time averages and imbalances. Even though our approach is generic, we focus on two paradigmatic models-a lossy Bose-Hubbard lattice and a dissipative two-spin system, where we investigate the role of quantum jumps and interactions in the Liouvillian spectrum, in terms of complex and structured pseudospectra. Our results demonstrate how non-Hermitian phenomena emerge in realistic quantum lattices, providing a bridge between classical EP physics and experimentally accessible open quantum systems.

papers.title: Step-isometries on Banach spaces
papers.abstract: Step-isometries are maps preserving the integer part of pairwise distances on metric spaces. They arise naturally in the study of infinite random geometric graphs, where graph isomorphisms between LARG-type random graphs reduce to step-isometries on the underlying vertex sets. Several fundamental open problems concerning the rigidity, extendability, and continuity of step-isometries were raised in recent literature, notably by Šemrl, and by Balogh, Walters, and Zsák. In the present paper we resolve a number of these long-standing open questions. We establish rigidity results for step-isometries defined on norm-dense subsets of both real and complex Banach spaces. For complex Banach spaces, we prove that every almost-surjective step-isometry on a norm-dense subset admits a unique extension to a surjective real-affine isometry of the whole space. In the real setting, we investigate three key properties $A$, $B$, $C$ formulated by Šemrl, which ask whether certain classes of step-isometries extend to surjective affine isometries. We verify these properties for uniformly non-square Banach spaces, for spaces with a dense set of Fréchet-smooth points, and for strictly convex Banach spaces with separable dual. In particular, we confirm Conjecture 2 due to Balogh, Walters, and Zsák without countability assumptions on the dense domain set. We further show that every bijective step-isometry defined on the entire Banach space is a homeomorphism, answering their Question 3 affirmatively. Specializing to $\ell_1^n$, we obtain that $\ell_1^n$ satisfies Property $A$ for all integers $n\ge 3$, settling an open problem posed by Šemrl.

papers.title: Helical magnetism from sliding Luttinger liquids in hole-doped twisted bilayer WTe$_2$
papers.abstract: We investigate carrier-mediated helical magnetism in hole-doped twisted bilayer WTe$_2$ coupled to localized moments. The itinerant carriers are described by a valleyless two-flavor sliding Luttinger liquid. Via the feedback mechanism of the helical order formed within individual channels, we show that the interchannel spin susceptibility mediates a Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida interaction between localized moments that can stabilize a coherent helical magnetic texture across the coupled-wire array. A spin-wave analysis of the ordered state allows us to estimate the magnon energies and helix-ordering scale. The magnon energies depend on the carrier interactions with representative values falling in the microwave regime, suggesting possible detection by magnetic-resonance techniques. The helical order partially gaps the carrier spectrum and renormalizes the spin-correlation and relaxation exponents. These results identify twisted bilayer WTe$_2$ as a tunable low-dimensional platform for realizing and probing carrier-mediated helical magnetism.

papers.title: A Hybrid Digital/Analog Polyphase Filtering Approach for High-Speed RF-DACs
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid polyphase interpolation for RF-DACs that removes the need for full-rate digital commutation by using passive combining on the RF-DAC itself. A P-branch polyphase FIR filter is factored into M streams, each formed by a (P/M)-way digital commutator at fRF/M and driving a dedicated RF-DAC slice, giving either partial digital (1<M<P) or fully analog (M=P) recombination. We show that the slice array acts as a single full-rate DAC with an M-times longer zero-order hold, derive yield laws for slice gain, timing and unit-capacitor mismatch, and find that with retiming the binding requirement is sub-picosecond matching of the fRF clock arrival, so the best choice is the smallest M that closes digital timing. Two 28-nm digital macros, designed for a 12.8GSps output rate and verified by post-layout simulation, illustrate a 4-phase variant that closes timing up to 14.4GSps with its digital logic at fRF/4 and an 8-phase variant that closes timing up to 16GSps with its digital logic at fRF/8. The analog recombination is evaluated with a behavioral model of the slice array. The architectures target wideband software defined radio (SDR) platforms, including cognitive radio, electronic warfare, and satellite communications.

papers.title: Weighted \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal{O}$}-operators on pre-Leibniz algebras and post-pre-Leibniz structures
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce weighted $\mathcal{O}$-operators (also called weighted relative Rota-Baxter operators) on pre-Leibniz algebras. We construct a differential graded Lie algebra whose Maurer-Cartan elements are exactly these operators. This allows us to define their cohomology as that of the induced pre-Leibniz algebra with coefficients in a suitable representation. As an application, we study formal and finite order deformations of these operators. We show that this theory splits the corresponding theory for weighted $\mathcal{O}$-operators on Leibniz algebras. Finally, we introduce post-pre-Leibniz algebras as the algebraic structures underlying weighted $\mathcal{O}$-operators on pre-Leibniz algebras.

papers.title: Non-asymptotic First- and Second-Order Tail Brackets for the Kostlan-Shub-Smale Field and Spherical k-Spin Complexity
papers.abstract: For the Kostlan-Shub-Smale field $X$ of degree $k\ge3$ on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, we prove the two-sided bound $(1-\varepsilon(u))\,δ_{*}(u)\le\mathbb{P}\{\sup X>u\}\leδ_{*}(u)$ at every finite $(k,d)$, where $δ_{*}(u)$ is the expected number of critical points above $u$, halved when $k$ is even, and $\varepsilon(u)$ is explicit for $ρu\ge\min\{d-1,\frac32\sqrt{2(d-1)}\}$. The gap is therefore at most of order $e^{-(1+ρ^{2})u^{2}/2}$ with $ρ^{2}=k/(2(k-1))$. We also give $δ_{*}$ itself in closed form, as a finite sum of Hermite polynomials, together with a two-term envelope that is asymptotically sharp and a single-monomial relaxation of the form $Cu^{d-2}e^{-u^{2}/2}$. As an application we bracket the annealed complexity of the spherical $k$-spin Hamiltonian at every finite $(k,d)$: the upper bound holds at every energy, a lower bound of the same form at every energy above $9/4$ times the spectral edge $\sqrt{2(d-1)}/ρ$, above twice the edge when $d\ge10$, and is consistent with the Auffinger-Ben Arous-Černý complexity function as $d\to\infty$.

papers.title: Left-Right-Consistent Iterative Stereo Matching via Cross-Injection
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art stereo matching models predominantly predict the disparity of only the left (reference) view. However, applications such as per-eye AR/VR rendering, novel view synthesis, or two-view depth fusion require disparity for both views, and need those two maps to agree. The usual workaround of running the network a second time on the horizontally flipped and swapped pair gives two independent predictions that can be inconsistent, especially on transparent surfaces, in textureless regions, and at occlusion boundaries. We introduce cross-injection (CI), a lightweight extension for iterative (refinement-based) models that can be added to any pretrained left-only iterative matcher. It couples the two passes by injecting the explicit, signed left-right inconsistency as an additional input cue at every step of the refinement stage. We empirically show that CI substantially reduces left-right disagreement on every benchmark (more than halving it on Booster for FoundationStereo), while largely preserving sharp object boundaries. Furthermore, using two state-of-the-art stereo matching models, we show that CI also reduces the single-view disparity error, making it a worthwhile extension even if only left disparity is needed.

papers.title: Definitions, Label Names, or Demonstrations? Auditing What Governs LLM Annotation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to annotate social-science texts, but high accuracy does not establish that they apply researcher-supplied category definitions: predictions may instead reflect prior associations with category labels or labeled demonstrations. We introduce a counterfactual audit that reassigns definitions among output labels, distinguishing adherence to supplied definitions from preservation of a dataset's original mapping. Across three political-text datasets, models rarely follow reassigned definitions, and standard fine-tuning strengthens the original mapping without reliably increasing definition adherence. We then study retrieval-augmented annotation. Retrieving the nearest training examples generally outperforms retrieving examples separately within each category despite using fewer demonstrations. On the two tasks with substantial gains, direct \(k\)-nearest-neighbor classification recovers 74--93\% of the improvement, indicating that neighborhood labels provide much of the predictive signal. Relabeling fixed demonstrations redirects predictions, whereas aligning demonstrations with reassigned definitions substantially increases adherence to the new mapping. Thus, accuracy-improving interventions need not increase codebook adherence; definitions, category labels, demonstrations, retrieval, and training data should be aligned and validated jointly.

papers.title: Increased Crystal Nucleation in the Glassy State of a Polymer/Water Mixture
papers.abstract: Within classical nucleation theory, crystal nucleation requires sufficient supersaturation, but is suppressed at low temperatures due to reduced molecular mobility, leading to a maximum nucleation rate typically above the glass transition temperature $T_g$. Here, we experimentally show that this conventional picture breaks down in a biocompatible polymer poly(2-methoxyethyl acrylate)(PMEA)/water mixture. We find that the number of nuclei increases dramatically below $T_g$, with the effective nucleation rate exhibiting an unusual maximum at approximately $T_g-10$ K. Calorimetric experiments reveal a strong temperature-history dependence of cold crystallization of water in hydrated PMEA, which is explained by the observed nucleation behavior. We propose that the unusual enhancement of nucleation below $T_g$ provides a key mechanism linking high glass-forming ability and cold crystallization upon heating, thereby explaining the striking asymmetry in crystallization behavior between cooling and heating. Our findings suggest that a hidden nucleation-rate maximum below $T_g$ may also underlie cold crystallization in other glass-forming liquids.

papers.title: Overview of the ImageCLEFmedical 2026 GANs task: Exploring fingerprint detection, privacy leakage, and synthetic medical image generation
papers.abstract: The 2026 ImageCLEFmedical GANs Task Exploring Fingerprint Detection, Privacy Leakage, and Synthetic Medical Image Generation continues to investigate privacy and security concerns around using patient data to generate synthetic medical images, now in its fourth edition. This edition introduces three complementary subtasks: the first extends prior editions by asking participants to detect which real images were used in training a Generative Adversarial Network to produce given synthetic outputs; the second is a novel subtask requiring participants to identify which latent vector produced each synthetic image, probing the faithfulness and reversibility of the latent-to-image mapping; the third asks participants to generate privacy-preserving CT slices, quantifying the trade-off between image fidelity and patient privacy. Ground-truth annotations and benchmark datasets of real and GAN-generated lung CT slices are provided for all subtasks. Evaluation is based on Cohen's Kappa for Subtask 1, matching accuracy for Subtask 2, and a combination of FID and Privacy Preservation Score (PPS) for Subtask 3. Overall, 37 teams registered for the task, with 10 teams submitting runs across subtasks and 6 teams submitting working notes papers. This paper presents an overview of the task setup, datasets, evaluation metrics, and summarises the approaches and results of participating teams.

papers.title: From LoRA to Language: Recovering Skill Documents from Adapters
papers.abstract: Agent skills are short documents that teach a language model how to handle a class of tasks. To save context, these documents are increasingly compiled into low-rank adapters (LoRA), which keep the behaviour but lose the text: an adapter is hard to read, edit, audit or move to another model. We ask whether the skill document can be written back from the adapter and its frozen base model, and we score each recovered document by the share of the original's key instructions it states and by the tasks it solves. Reading the weights alone recovered little with the methods we tried; a learned map from weights to text passed on about one bit of the document. Running the adapter worked much better. The Executing Writer, a small writer trained on top of the adapted model, recovers 39-44% of the key instructions of held-out skills, against 1.3-1.5% with another skill's adapter, and on adapters fitted to 41 external skills its documents restore 85-91% of the original's task gain. These strongest results are on adapters whose training stored the document; adapters trained on behaviour alone are much harder for trained writers (1-2% of instructions). For these adapters we test an agent that runs the base and adapted models and writes a skill from where they differ. On ALFWorld its skills recover 58-71% of a LoRA's gain and carry over to models that cannot load the LoRA, lifting Llama-3.1-8B from 5% to 55%. Whether such a skill comes from the adapter depends on what the adapter learned: when its behaviour cannot be guessed, the adapter is the source; when it can, a reward loop without the adapter does as well.

papers.title: Every countable group has the nonsingular weak Rokhlin property
papers.abstract: We prove that for every countable group $Γ$, in the space of nonsingular actions by $Γ$, there is an action whose orbit under conjugation is dense. This is the nonsingular analogue of the result of Glasner, Thouvenot, and Weiss that every countable group $Γ$ is weak Rokhlin, i.e., there is a dense orbit in the space of probability measure preserving $Γ$-actions.

papers.title: Optimal robust comonotonic risk sharing under operational constraints
papers.abstract: Risk-sharing arrangements such as reinsurance programs and catastrophe pools must satisfy operational constraints, including capacity limits, attachment bands, retention rules and cession limits. Under distortion risk measures, the unconstrained optimum assigns each loss layer to the participant for whom that layer is least costly, but operational constraints break this layerwise rule, and there is no general method to compute the constrained optimum. We show that, for comonotonic allocations, the participants' distortion risk measures and the operational constraints are linear in the amount of each loss layer held by each participant, so the constrained risk-sharing problem on a discretized loss is a linear program that standard software can solve. Its dual gives supporting prices for the loss layers and the marginal value of relaxing each operational constraint. Where the set of binding constraints changes, the constrained optimal value can have a kink, and the smallest and largest optimal multipliers then give the one-sided effects of relaxing and tightening a constraint. To protect the allocation against disagreement between loss models, we also consider the robust version of the risk-sharing problem, that is, minimizing the worst-case total risk assessment over finitely many probability scenarios. This robust problem is again a linear program, and we quantify the cost of protection against model uncertainty from its optimal value. We illustrate the approach with a catastrophe reinsurance tower.

papers.title: Scalable BLE Channel Sounding Localization with Ranging-Assisted PDoA
papers.abstract: Bluetooth Channel Sounding (CS) enables accurate phase-based ranging, but multi-anchor localization requires sequential ranging exchanges that limit scalability and increase measurement latency. This paper proposes Ranging-Assisted Phase Difference of Arrival (RA-PDoA), a scalable BLE localization architecture combining one active anchor performing a standard two-way CS exchange with multiple passive receive-only anchors observing the same transmissions. A channel-recovery framework is derived that enables passive anchors to reconstruct a channel response suitable for super-resolution delay estimation, allowing multipath-robust ranging without participating in a two-way exchange. Coarse arrival-time information is further used to bound the position estimate and reject inconsistent range solutions. A comprehensive evaluation characterizes the impact of multipath propagation, body shadowing, synchronization requirements, oscillator impairments, anchor placement, and deployment inaccuracies, thereby quantifying the practical infrastructure requirements for scalable BLE localization. Simulation results in modeled indoor environments show that RA-PDoA reduces the 90th-percentile localization error from 175.3 cm to 95.5 cm under body shadowing while maintaining an airtime requirement independent of the number of anchors. The results demonstrate that a single active ranging link enables scalable and multipath-robust BLE Channel Sounding localization.

papers.title: Symmetry-Resolved Criticality in Dissipative Quantum Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Symmetry breaking in mixed quantum states exhibits a rich strong-to-weak hierarchy, yet the use of symmetry as an operational probe of dissipative criticality remains largely unexplored. In this work, we develop a symmetry-based framework that connects semiclassical phase space, trajectory-level dynamics, and ensemble responses, and demonstrate it in the two-dimensional dissipative XYZ model. We show that symmetry breaking manifests semiclassically as a bifurcation of the Husimi-Q distribution and dynamically as a sharp change in a trajectory-level symmetry residual. At the ensemble level, the weak-symmetry sensitivity to a perturbed symmetry operator exhibits pronounced finite-size scaling, yielding an estimate of the dissipative critical point. Finally, we propose a trajectory-based quantum-circuit algorithm in which mid-circuit measurements condition quantum jumps and allow the proposed indicators to be extracted from circuit observables. Our work provides a symmetry-centered route to diagnosing dissipative phase transitions and critical scaling in open quantum many-body systems.

papers.title: CO gaps in cold transition disks around low-mass stars
papers.abstract: Transition disks with large inner dust cavities are promising targets to study planet formation, as these disks are likely hosting massive planetary companions. The structure of gas and dust inside the cavity are crucial for understanding the potential of planet formation in the regions. We investigate the structure of gas and dust in a sample of three cold, inclined transition disks around K and M stars without evidence for an inner dusty disk. We present new high-resolution ALMA Band 6 data of both 230 GHz continuum at 0.02" (~3 au) resolution and the 12CO 2-1, 13CO 2-1, C18O 2-1 isotopologues at 0.12" (~20 au) resolution. We analyze the radial profiles, compute the brightness temperatures, and derive estimates of the gas and dust content of the inner disk at 1 au. All three disks show dust cavities of 30-40 au in radius. The CO emission extends inside the cavity with progressively smaller CO cavity radii for the more abundant isotopologues. The 13CO brightness temperature profile is similar to that of other transition disks and full disks. No inner dust disk is detected in the ALMA continuum, consistent with the lack of near-infrared excess. Considering the accretion rates, the gas-to-dust ratio in the inner disk at 1 au is estimated to be as high as 10^5. No significant differences in the brightness temperature or in the gas-to-dust ratio are found between our disks and other transition disks around more luminous stars, contrary to expectations. This highlights the importance of individual-target studies through thermochemical modeling or multi-transition analyses to constrain the dust and gas structures in the cavity. The observed disk structures could be explained by super-Jovian companion on eccentric orbits, but further modeling is needed to confirm this conclusion.

papers.title: Not All Entropy Is Equal: Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
papers.abstract: Policy entropy is widely used to diagnose exploration and collapse in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), yet its magnitude does not consistently track reasoning performance across optimization objectives. We argue that this ambiguity arises because global token entropy conflates uncertainty in successful and failed trajectories, diversity across correct solution strategies, and variation among realizations of the same strategy. We introduce \textbf{Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation (RCEA)}, a hierarchical diagnostic framework that separates complete-trajectory entropy from average token entropy, conditions uncertainty on verifier outcome and process validity, measures correct-solution-mode retention, and connects these population-level quantities to local covariance-driven updates. In controlled sweeps over six RLVR objectives at two model scales, entropy trajectories do not induce a stable ordering of reasoning accuracy. Token entropy is higher for verifier-failed than successful trajectories under both broad separately aggregated estimates and a common-question paired analysis, whose confidence intervals exclude equality at 10 of 12 displayed endpoints. A local covariance approximation predicts the direction of adjacent-checkpoint entropy change in 95.5\% of nonfailed transitions; a reward-stratified endpoint proxy further shows that positive chosen-token covariance is more tail-concentrated within failed prefixes. Every reportable trained endpoint exhibits some contraction in independently audited correct-solution-mode breadth, whose positive association with large-\(k\) coverage remains exploratory. These results show that entropy collapse should be diagnosed by which uncertainty is removed, rather than by global entropy alone.

papers.title: Additive $Ω(\log^* OPT)$ Gap for Bin Packing with Three Items per Bin
papers.abstract: We prove that bin packing is NP-hard to approximate within an additive factor of $o(\ls\OPT)$, even when all item sizes are arbitrarily close to $1/3$. This gives the first lower bound for bin packing with an additive factor that depends explicitly on the optimum value. In addition, we give a polynomial-time reduction from any bin packing instance into one with item sizes arbitrarily close to $1/3$, preserving its additive configuration-LP gap up to constant factors. Thus, in the sense of additive configuration LP gap and up to a constant, we confirm the conjecture that 3-partition instances are the hardest bin packing instances. In particular, we obtain an unconditional $Ω(\ls\OPT)$ gap for 3-partition instances. We build on the recent OpenAI construction that uses five items per bin and rules out any constant additive gap.

papers.title: Logit Laundering: Evading Data-Use Auditing in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Data-use auditing in Large Language Models (LLMs) aims to determine whether the given data has been used for training, thereby supporting data ownership safeguards. A dominant solution is data watermarking, which embeds traceable signals into training data and detects them in model outputs. Recent studies have proposed many watermarking-based auditing methods in LLMs. However, systematic investigation from an adversarial perspective remains limited: non-compliant LLM providers would use unauthorized copyrighted datasets for training their own models to enhance model capabilities, while attempting to evade detection by auditors, thereby avoiding legal liability. To fill this research gap, we propose a novel evasion framework, termed Logit Laundering, where the non-compliant LLM provider manipulates model outputs at inference time to undermine detectable watermark signals. Specifically, we design a logit reshaping module to suppress watermark-induced statistical signals by integrating a statistical bias estimator as a plug-and-play component. This design keeps the model parameters unchanged and performs manipulation only in the logit space, thereby enabling auditing evasion while minimizing the impact on model's learned knowledge. To further balance evasion effectiveness and model utility, we introduce a confidence-aware scaling module to adaptively calibrate the suppression strength based on next-token prediction confidence. Extensive evaluations show that Logit Laundering can successfully evade existing various state-of-the-art auditing methods, significantly attenuating detectable signals, while preserving model utility on downstream tasks. Our work highlights the need for exploring more robust auditing methods to guard against evasion behaviors.

papers.title: Incentive Pathologies in a Live LLM Agent Arena: An Empirical Study of Concentration, Reward-Rule Implementation Discrepancy, and Network Dilution
papers.abstract: We audit one live LLM agent arena (AITRAP; 22 autonomous agent seats, ~96,000 reasoning nodes) over nine days (Oct 16-25, 2026), during which the platform deployed two bundled incentive changes: a progressive tax reform (V2.9.3, Oct 19) and a seed-inversion with explorer-side action update (V3.0, Oct 21). These serve as before-and-after markers, not cleanly isolated interventions. Four exploratory predictions are tested against ten data frames (F1-F10) using the Gini coefficient, Top-K concentration share, code-level reconstruction of the continuation-bonus mechanism, and the Mann-Kendall trend test. The Gini analysis is inconclusive at 95% confidence (bootstrap intervals straddle 0.7). The Top-4 node-activity-score share falls from 97.2% (Oct 19, pre-V2.9.3) to 49.4% (Oct 25, post-V3.0; 56.7% under a merge-seat assumption). The continuation bonus, announced as depth-based x10, resolves at code level to a four-condition anti-abuse gate paying x2.85 in the typical case and permanently blocking the self-continuation it superficially rewards; the gate was active ~40 hours before the V3.0 announcement. The events-per-node ratio declines significantly (Mann-Kendall S=-45, z=-3.94, p=8.3e-5) from 7.36 to 7.069. We discuss implications for incentive designers, the announcement-implementation gap, and public peer review as an event record.

papers.title: Isolated yet highly unstable 2D Euler equilibria
papers.abstract: We construct steady solutions of the two-dimensional Euler equations on smooth annular domains that are isolated, modulo scaling, in the $L^\infty$ vorticity topology. They are highly unstable: any Yudovich trajectory remaining sufficiently close to such an equilibrium on an open time interval is a stationary multiple of it and, moreover, at fixed energy, enstrophy and circulations, distinct nearby trajectories cannot return even weakly to the equilibrium. Further, on any non-circular annulus, we show that this kind of isolated, highly unstable equilibria occurs arbitrarily close in the Yudovich norm to smooth equilibria which are themselves non-isolated.

papers.title: Sharp isoperimetry in groups of polynomial growth
papers.abstract: We study weighted edge boundary and outer vertex boundary on Cayley graphs of polynomial growth of degree $Q>1$. For every finite symmetric generating set, we prove that each exact isoperimetric profile satisfies $I(n)=c n^{(Q-1)/Q}+O(n^{(Q-1)/Q-β})$, where $β=1/(8Q^2)$. We identify the leading constant with the isoperimetric constant of a horizontal perimeter on the limiting Carnot group, after accounting for the counting density. Its integrand is a norm with polyhedral unit ball, determined by a convex minimization with one real variable for each coset of a torsion-free nilpotent subgroup. For every asymptotically minimizing sequence, we translate its vertex sets so that the characteristic functions of the associated rescaled regions are precompact in $L^1$. The limiting regions minimize continuum perimeter at fixed volume. The exact-cardinality estimate requires no regularity assumption on these regions. For virtually abelian groups, we prove a quantitative stability estimate using a discrete approximation to the Euclidean Wulff body. The relative symmetric difference from a translate is bounded by the square root of the sum of the relative boundary deficit and a cardinality error. We also characterize when bounded additive changes of Cayley metric preserve the leading vertex constant. Failure occurs already in rank two; we construct pairs with the same measured asymptotic cone whose leading constants have an unbounded ratio as the rank grows.

papers.title: Yang-Mills theories with scalar matter: a first foray using the Curci-Ferrari model
papers.abstract: The Curci-Ferrari (CF) model provides an efficient perturbative framework for describing several aspects of the infrared (IR) dynamics of Yang-Mills (YM) theories. We extend this framework to YM theories coupled with scalar matter and investigate its main properties, with particular emphasis on the one-loop two-point correlation functions of scalars, gluons, and ghosts. We analyze the renormalization group (RG) structure of the model, computing its beta functions and studying the corresponding RG flows for different scalar masses. We establish the existence of IR-safe trajectories along which perturbation theory remains under control and identify a novel fixed-point, while recovering the standard CF results in an appropriate limit. We then confront our results with lattice data through a simultaneous fit of the scalar, gluon, and ghost propagators, finding excellent agreement. Our results indicate that, within the approximations considered here, the CF framework gives a successful perturbative description of the IR regime of YM theories coupled with scalar matter.

papers.title: Reconstructing intracell polarization with calibrated sapphire-window optics for collimated blue-light generation in a rubidium cell
papers.abstract: We study the polarization dependence of collimated blue light (CBL) generated near 420~nm by resonant four-wave mixing in thermal rubidium vapor in a sapphire-window cell driven at 780 and 776~nm. Sapphire windows can transform the polarization of pump light before it reaches the vapor, complicating the interpretation of polarization-dependent nonlinear emission. We measured the 780-nm pump Stokes state at an external before-cell reference plane to calibrate the common HWP/QWP preparation optics and recorded 266 off-resonant external output Stokes states after the complete sapphire-window rubidium cell at 90, 100, and 110~$^\circ$C in two propagation orientations. Direct paired-wavelength measurements show a mean before-cell 780/776 separation of $4.29^\circ$ and temperature- and orientation-specific complete-cell rotations of $22.20^\circ$--$32.02^\circ$, with rms residuals of $4.83^\circ$--$12.87^\circ$. Using this calibrated co-prepared pump description, we analyzed 2574 measurements of total spectrally filtered 420-nm CBL intensity. Across the six temperature--orientation data sets, a complete nine-coefficient second-order response yielded cross-validated $R^2$ values of 0.636 to 0.828. These paired-wavelength measurements establish, for each temperature--orientation data set, a fixed relative Stokes-space map between the two co-prepared pump trajectories, with the residual of this mapping defining the experimental uncertainty of the correlated two-pump reduction used in the response model. Thus, the resulting framework combines a reconstructed vapor-entrance polarization coordinate with direct two-wavelength calibration of the assembled cell and provides a practical basis for polarization-controlled nonlinear-optical experiments in sapphire-window vapor cells.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of solutions to the critical $p$-Laplace equation near isolated singularities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of weak solutions to the following critical $p$-Laplace equation \[ -Δ_p u=u^{p^*-1}, \quad u\ge0 \quad\hbox{in }B_1\setminus\{0\}, \] where $Δ_pu=\diver(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u)$ is the classical $p$-Laplacian with $1<p<n$, $p^*=\frac{np}{n-p}$ is the Sobolev critical exponent and $B_1\setminus\{0\}\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is the punctured unit ball. We develop a nonlinear potential-theoretic method to establish sharp upper bounds for solutions, without using the method of moving planes or moving spheres. Furthermore, we use Steiner symmetrization to study the radial symmetry of global singular solutions, and thereby classify all Fowler singular solutions. Finally, we prove that every local singular solution is asymptotic to a global Fowler singular solution.

papers.title: FlexRL: an R package for Flexible Record Linkage and Linked Data Quality Assessment
papers.abstract: FlexRL is an R package for probabilistic record linkage and inference on linked data. It provides a method to link observations from the same entities across two data sources that lack a unique identifier but share partially identifying variables. This method fits a hierarchical latent variable model of the data generation process, rather than classifying pairs of records from the comparison of their values, and accommodates registration errors and variables changing over time. Since linkage may affect subsequent analyses, the package also provides tools to assess the linked data quality as functions of the linkage decision rule. Two false discovery proportion estimators are implemented: a probabilistic approach contingent on the record linkage model and an augmented approach relying on an auxiliary estimation using synthetic data. Several measures of divergence of the linked sample from the source population are provided. These tools are agnostic to the underlying record linkage model and can be applied to any method. Together, they connect the output of the linkage to the validity of the subsequent analyses. The implementation combines standard R functions and S3 methods with Rcpp computations, resulting in fast execution times and a low memory footprint.

papers.title: Trace and Regularized Index of Callias Operators on Hyperbolic Space
papers.abstract: Let $d \geq 3$ be odd. On hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$, we consider Callias-type operators, i.e. Dirac-Schrödinger operators of the form $D = ic \nabla + A$, where $c \nabla$ is the Dirac operator and $A$ a function with values in the self-adjoint operators, and provide an explicit formula for the iterated trace $\text{tr}_{L^2(\mathbb{H}^d,H)} \text{tr}_{S}( e^{-tD^*D} - e^{-tDD^*})$, $t>0$, that appears in the formulation of the Witten index. Thereby, the operator $D$ is not assumed to be Fredholm.

papers.title: Different exact-law formulations to calculate the energy cascade rate in magnetohydrodynamic turbulence with and without mean magnetic fields
papers.abstract: At scales much larger than the ion inertial length and ion-gyroscale, space-plasma turbulence is often described within the framework of incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). Using high-resolution direct numerical simulations with $1024^3$ grid points, we perform the first systematic numerical comparison of three exact-law formulations for the total energy cascade in homogeneous, but not necessarily isotropic, MHD turbulence: the Yaglom-Monin (YM), Banerjee-Galtier (BG), and two-point correlator formulations. Despite directional variations, the angle-averaged energy transfer rates for all three formulations show excellent agreement for zero, moderate, and strong background magnetic fields. These results clearly suggest the usefulness of alternative BG and correlator formulations for estimating the energy cascade rates in turbulent space plasmas when the required spatial derivatives are accessible through multi-spacecraft measurements. We also argue that the isotropic Politano-Pouquet (PP) formulation does not provide a true directional transfer rate and therefore its application as a single-direction energy transfer rate estimator leads to inaccurate values, especially under anisotropic conditions. Decomposing the exact formulations into RMHD and non-RMHD contributions, we also show that the RMHD cascade rates cannot be obtained merely by increasing the strength of the mean magnetic field in incompressible magnetohydrodynamic turbulence. Finally, a term-by-term analysis of different formulations reveals how different nonlinear interaction channels coexist and collaborate with each other to maintain the same energy cascade rate across the inertial scales.

papers.title: The Role Of Recurrent Refinement In Medical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: While feed-forward segmentation networks perform well on large cohorts, they degrade in constrained clinical settings with few training samples and imaging artifacts. Human vision, by contrast, remains robust under these conditions, a property partly attributed to the recurrent and feedback connectivity of the visual cortex, which refines visual information over time. Inspired by this, we append lightweight recurrent refinement blocks to segmentation backbones, namely Conditional Random Fields (CRFs), modern Hopfield networks and convolutional GRUs, and study their behaviour as the number of iterations increases at test time (including beyond the training horizon). Evaluated on two open-source datasets, Kvasir- SEG and ARCADE, our recurrent blocks add less than 1.5% parameters and yield gains on clean data (up to 1.4 pp) and under noise (up to 17 pp) while reducing HD95. Code is available at https://github.com/joaodsmarques/recurrencehelpsegmentation .

papers.title: Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS) for Air-Ground Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC)
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a multi-user single-target air-ground integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, in which a ground pinching-antenna system (PASS) transmits communication and sensing signals and an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) receives the target echo. The communication and sensing beamforming vectors, pinching antenna positions, and UAV position are jointly optimized to minimize the weighted Cramér-Rao bound (CRB). A penalty dual decomposition (PDD) algorithm is developed for the resulting nonconvex problem. The auxiliary variable and beamforming subproblems admit globally optimal solutions in semi-closed form, while the positions of the pinching antennas and the UAV are updated by successive convex approximation (SCA). Under mild conditions, every accumulation point of the sequence generated by our proposed algorithm is a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point of the reformulated problem. Numerical results show that the proposed PASS-UAV design achieves a lower weighted CRB than conventional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) and PASS benchmarks.

papers.title: Optimal performance of driven-dissipative many-body quantum batteries beyond complete nonreciprocity
papers.abstract: Proposals for nonreciprocal quantum batteries identify the point of complete nonreciprocity, where coherent and reservoir-mediated couplings balance, as the operating point for enhanced charging. We show that, for batteries built from interacting qubits, this point is, in general, suboptimal. The optimal design is set by a more intricate interplay between the coherent coupling and the local and collective dissipation rates, of which complete nonreciprocity is only a special case. We consider a many-body battery charged by a driven many-body charger, with each qubit coupled to a local bath and the complete setup immersed in a shared engineered reservoir. For a weakly driven two-qubit setup, we prove the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction to be the optimal coupling, and show that the battery capacity is maximized at a coupling strength fixed by the local and collective dissipation rates, which coincides with complete nonreciprocity only for a specific balance between them. The shared reservoir enhances the capacity for couplings weaker or stronger than both local dissipation rates, and can increase the extractable work even where it reduces the capacity. At strong drive, with the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction between the charger and the battery, the capacity is bounded by $1/2$. For qubits arranged in a star network with a single central battery qubit, these results remain qualitatively unchanged, while the maximum capacity of a battery charged by $N_A$ weakly driven charger qubits saturates with $N_A$ in the presence of the shared reservoir, approaching its limit as $N_A^{-1}$. In contrast, the maximum capacity of $N_B$ qubit batteries charged by a single-qubit charger decays as $N_B^{-2}$.

papers.title: DexDICE: Reconciling Safety and Performance via Dual-Expert Offline Imitation Learning
papers.abstract: Ensuring high returns while providing strong safety guarantees in offline imitation learning (IL) is a fundamental challenge: existing approaches either rely on explicitly specified cost functions, which are difficult to design for complex real-world safety constraints, or require expert demonstrations that are both safe and high-performing, which are often too costly to collect. We introduce dual-expert imitation learning, which leverages two complementary data sources: (i) safety-compliant demonstrations that faithfully follow safety guidelines but may be suboptimal, and (ii) performance-oriented demonstrations that achieve high returns but may violate safety guidelines. To address this problem, we propose DexDICE (Dual-expert offline imitation learning via stationary DIstribution Correction Estimation). Instead of conventional distribution constraints, DexDICE combines DICE-style offline learning with safe support constraints, enabling agents to exploit high-return behaviors while remaining within safety-compliant regions. We prove that the ideal solution satisfying this constraint exactly has zero unsafe-region visitation with high probability. We evaluate DexDICE on a re-curated DSRL benchmark and validate it on a real-world mobile-robot navigation task trained directly from human teleoperation demonstrations, where it substantially outperforms baselines and remains robust to data scarcity and quality degradation.

papers.title: A hybrid model for zero-inflated proportion data
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid model for analyzing zero-inflated proportion data by distinguishing two types of zeros. The first type arises from sampling variability, whereas the second reflects intrinsically unsuitable covariates. Accordingly, the hybrid model combines a regression component for suitable observations with an estimator of the suitability region that identifies unsuitable covariates. Using a debiasing technique, we establish the consistency of both the regression and classification components, together with the asymptotic normality of the regression coefficient and a convergence rate for the support estimator. Comprehensive simulation studies verify our theoretical findings. We further apply the model to two real datasets, where it outperforms most competing methods.

papers.title: Debias Online Expectile Regression for High-Dimensional Stream Data and Statistic Inference
papers.abstract: Expectile regression is a powerful tool for capturing heterogeneous structures in data and has attracted increasing attention in large-scale data analysis due to its computational efficiency. However, statistical inference for high-dimensional online expectile regression remains underexplored. In this paper, we propose a debiased online expectile regression method for high-dimensional streaming data. The proposed method incorporates Lasso regularization to perform variable selection and alleviate estimation instability caused by high dimensionality. It further adopts an online updating strategy in which recursively updated cumulative statistics are used to approximate the global gradient, and a proximal gradient descent algorithm is employed to update model parameters. To enable valid inference when only the current batch and historical summary statistics are available, we also develop an online precision matrix estimation procedure. We establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed debiased estimator. Extensive numerical studies and real-data applications show that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to the oracle and offline estimators while maintaining low storage cost.

papers.title: EDP-PI-DOSnet: An Energy Dissipation Preserving Neural Solver for Two-Phase Flow Problems
papers.abstract: Preserving the energy dissipation properties of gradient flow equations is important for the stability and reliability of numerical approximations, particularly in long-time simulations. In this paper, we propose a class of energy-dissipation-preserving physics-informed deep operator splitting networks (EDP-PI-DOSnets) for solving gradient flow equations. The proposed framework incorporates classical structure-preserving numerical schemes into neural network architectures, allowing the corresponding discrete energy dissipation laws to be preserved. In particular, suitable constraints are imposed on the convolution kernels to ensure that the learned discrete operators are symmetric and negative semidefinite. Furthermore, several network formulations are developed based on the Crank--Nicolson (CN), scalar auxiliary variable Crank--Nicolson (SAV/CN), and relaxed discrete variational derivative (R-DVD-1) schemes. Meanwhile, a physics-informed loss function based on the residuals of the governing equations is employed. Numerical experiments show that the predicted solutions are in good agreement with the reference solutions while satisfying the corresponding discrete energy dissipation laws. The results also suggest stable behavior during long-time recursive prediction and the potential applicability of the proposed framework to two-phase flow problems.

papers.title: Navigating Selection Bias in Genome-wide Association Studies (GWAS)
papers.abstract: Selection bias arises when inclusion in a genetic study depends on traits, or causes of traits, that are associated with genotype. It is present in volunteer-based biobanks, case-control designs and studies of disease progression, and genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from affected samples can propagate this bias into post-GWAS analyses, such as polygenic scores (PGS), Mendelian randomization (MR) and genetic correlation analyses. Despite this broad potential impact, selection bias is sometimes ignored in genetic studies. Many methods exist to detect and correct it, but they rely on different assumptions and require specific data. We organise ten methods applicable to GWAS by the decisions an analyst faces: whether to diagnose or correct, which data are available (individual-level or summary-level), and which form of selection is operating (non-representative participation, case-control ascertainment, index events, sex-differential participation or survival to recruitment). For each method, we describe its principle and assumptions, and we compare methods addressing the same form of selection by their assumptions, data requirements and limitations. A companion GitHub repository implements nine methods in R, prepares input for the external SPREG software, and provides worked examples on simulated data with known true effects for each form of selection, one of which we present in full. An interactive tool supports method selection. We conclude with recommendations for bias-aware study design, sensitivity analysis and reporting.

papers.title: Kolmogorov Obstacle Problems: Euclidean Free Boundary Regularity under a Cone Condition
papers.abstract: We study obstacle problems for Kolmogorov-type operators that diffuse in one variable and transport in another. Such problems describe American options on running averages. Under a cone estimate, a strong monotonicity condition on the solution in the diffusive direction, we show that the free boundary is a graph in the diffusive direction with Hölder continuous first derivatives in the Euclidean sense, and that every free boundary point is regular. The key observation is that a Euclidean Lipschitz free boundary is flat at the intrinsic scale. For the American fixed-strike Asian option we verify the cone estimate, so that its exercise boundary has the same regularity.

papers.title: Fluctuations of heat kernels and exit times on random graphs and application to the critical long-range percolation
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph equipped with random conductance. We give sufficient conditions for the Markov chain on $\mathcal{G}$ to exhibit large scale fluctuations in its on-diagonal heat kernel and in exit times. The conditions also imply non-tightness of the height process w.r.t. the quenched measure, while it is tight w.r.t. the annealed measure. As an application of the general theory, we prove large scale fluctuations for the simple random walk on $1$-dimensional critical long-range percolation.

papers.title: Robust Bayes-like estimation of the distribution of a determinantal process
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the distribution of a determinantal process (DP) on a measured space from the observation of $n$ independent copies of it. Our estimator is obtained by sampling from a $T$-posterior distribution associated with a suitable prior, and we establish non-asymptotic risk bounds for the Hellinger loss which hold with high probability. These bounds remain valid when the data are only independent rather than i.i.d., and when the model is misspecified, which makes the estimator robust, for instance, to the presence of a small fraction of outliers. For determinantal projection processes of rank $k$ whose kernels are associated with $k$-dimensional subspaces of a $D$-dimensional space, Haar priors on Grassmannians lead to a rate of order $\sqrt{k(D-k)\log n/n}$, and model selection extends this result to infinite-dimensional settings. For general DPs, we introduce priors based on the spectral decomposition of the kernel that combine uniform distributions on the eigenvalues with Haar measures on Stiefel manifolds. When the underlying space is finite with $N$ elements, we obtain a rate of order $N\sqrt{\log n/n}$, without any assumption on the kernel, and derive that the $2^{N}$ principal minors of the kernel can be estimated simultaneously. Finally, for translation-invariant DPs on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, we obtain rates that only depend on the smoothness of the kernel at the origin and that are adaptive with respect to it. Combined with a new lower bound on the Hellinger distance between such DPs, these rates also yield estimators of the kernel in $\mathbb{L}_2$.

papers.title: The covariety of numerical semigroups with some prescribed pseudo-Frobenius numbers
papers.abstract: If $S$ is a numerical semigroup, then we denote by $m(S)$, $F(S)$ and $\mathrm{PF}(S)$ its multiplicity, its Frobenius number and its set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers, respectively. Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of positive integers. In this paper, we prove that $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{S\mid F(S)=\max(\mathcal P),\ \mathcal P\subseteq\mathrm{PF}(S)\}$ is a covariety.
